correctness.rationale: The graph, parallel open-neighborhood inhibition and first-hitting time are defined unambiguously. Same-part vertices sharing color evolve identically for all times, so 49 nonempty pairs of three-color supports exhaust all possible dynamics uniformly over arbitrary clique/independent sizes. Direct substitution of the transition gives the table; the only unbounded first-hitting case (clique only color 2, independent all three colors) is already a primitive 3-cycle. Surjection weights for 1, 2 and 3 occupied colors produce the exact first-time formulas, which sum to all 3^(m+n) states. The formal monomial certificate and independent exhaustive C++ check (923463 labelled configurations) both pass from packaged sources. Probability limits and uniformity follow algebraically by division. Verified sharpness includes n=1 and n>=2 boundaries; no probabilistic extrapolation is used.

value.rationale: Complete split graphs form a natural two-parameter family interpolating between star-like and densely joined modules. A complete first synchronization time distribution is a nontrivial dynamical invariant, not merely existence of synchronization. The 49-class exact reduction proves a sharp six-step cutoff and exposes a unique form of nonsynchronizing recurrent behavior; the exact probabilities give a uniform large-clique two-step concentration theorem. These extend beyond the star case and distinguish inhibition from other common three-state and binary graph dynamics.
